intention: Read today's journey to ponder the power of faith, sincere pursuit of truth, and how Allah grants success to those whose intentions are pure.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: In the heart of Persia, in the village of Jiyan in Isfahan, Salman al-Farsi grew up as an intelligent youth who loved knowledge, the son of the village chieftain and its wealthiest inhabitant. His father loved him immensely, even keeping him confined in the house out of fear for him. Salman exerted himself in Zoroastrianism, the religion of his people, until he became the custodian of the fire they worshipped, entrusted with the task of tending to it day and night. Yet, his heart was driven by a deep passion to search for the truth, refusing to blindly imitate what he found his ancestors upon.

steps.title: The Journey of Faith from Persia to Yathrib
steps.content:
One day, his father was preoccupied with matters concerning his estate and sent Salman to attend to its affairs. On his way, he passed by a Christian church and heard their voices in prayer. This caught his attention, and he entered to observe what they were doing. He admired their prayer and desired their religion, saying, "By Allah, this is better than that which we are upon." He remained with them until sunset and did not go to his father's estate. When he returned home, his father was alarmed by what he had done, imprisoned him, and put fetters on his legs out of fear that he would apostatize from his religion.

When the opportunity arose, Salman sent word to the Christians, saying: "If a caravan arriving from the land of Syria comes to you, let me know." Soon enough, a caravan arrived. He cleverly managed to loosen his fetters and escaped with them covertly to Syria. There, he asked about the most knowledgeable man in their religion, and they directed him to the bishop, the guardian of the church. Salman stayed with him, serving him and learning from him, but he soon discovered that the bishop was an evil man who commanded his followers to give charity while hoarding it for himself. When the bishop died, Salman exposed him to the Christians, whereupon they threw out his treasure, crucified him, and stoned him.

Then they appointed another man in his place. Salman stayed with him and found him to be the most ascetic of people regarding worldly life, the most desirous of the Hereafter, and the most constant in worship. Salman loved him dearly and stayed with him for a long time. When death approached the bishop, Salman asked him whom he should trust after him, and the bishop directed him to a man in Mosul. Salman traveled to Mosul and stayed with him, finding him upon the best state. When death approached him, he directed Salman to a man in Nusaybin. Salman then traveled to Nusaybin and stayed with him. When death approached him, he directed Salman to a man in Amorium. Thus, Salman moved among righteous scholars, one after another; whenever one of them died, he directed him to the next in an exhausting journey of searching for the truth.

When death approached his final companion in Amorium, Salman asked him whom he should follow. The man said to him, "My son, by Allah, I do not know of anyone upon the same state we were upon except a man who will emerge in the land of the Arabs. He is a prophet who eats the gift and does not eat charity, and between his shoulders is the seal of prophethood. If you are able to join him, then do so." Thus, after a long and arduous journey, Salman al-Farsi found what he was looking for and headed towards the land of Arabs, where he met the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. He found in him all the descriptions his teacher had given him, and he embraced Islam for the sake of Allah, the Lord of the Worlds, becoming one of the prominent companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and earning the title "Salman is one of us, the Ahl al-Bayt [Family of the House]."

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Sincerity in searching for the truth and seeking knowledge, and refusing blind imitation.
2. Steadfastness upon principle and sacrificing the precious and invaluable for the sake of faith.
3. Wisdom in distinguishing truth from falsehood and not being deceived by appearances.
4. That Allah grants success to those who have pure intentions in seeking guidance and eases for them the path of truth.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What are the challenges I face in my spiritual journey, and how can I draw inspiration from Salman al-Farsi's steadfastness and patience to overcome them, and be more sincere in my search for the truth?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will dedicate time to ponder upon Allah's cosmic and legislative signs, strive to increase my knowledge of my religion, emulate Salman's sincerity in seeking the truth, and pray to Allah to keep me steadfast upon the truth.

title: The Journey in Search of Truth
subtitle: The story of a noble knight who traversed the earth searching for the light of faith, finding it in Yathrib at the hands of the Master of Creation.
person: Salman al-Farsi (May Allah be pleased with him)
emotion: Sincerity, Patience, Steadfastness, Searching for Truth
heroQuote: «Peace be upon Salman al-Farsi on the day he arose to search for truth everywhere, and peace be upon him on the day he recognized the truth and believed in it with the firmest faith.»
intention: Read today's journey to ponder the greatness of sincerity in seeking the truth, how Allah guides whoever is sincere in searching for it, and to draw inspiration from Salman's patience and steadfastness.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Salman al-Farsi (May Allah be pleased with him) grew up in the village of 'Jayy' in Isfahan, a Persian Magian whose father was one of its chieftains and nobles, deeply fond of him to the extent of keeping him confined at home out of fear for him. However, Salman's heart inclined toward searching for the truth. One day, he went out to inspect his father's estate and passed by a Christian church. He entered it and was captivated by their prayers, marking the beginning of his long journey in search of the true religion.

steps.title: From Persia to Yathrib: The Story of Faith
steps.content:
After Salman found in Christianity that which resonated with his innate disposition, he fled from his father and homeland, traveling to the Levant to meet its monks. He met the first monk, staying with him to serve him and learn from him. When death approached the monk, he advised Salman to join another in Mosul. Thus, Salman moved among several monks in Mosul, then Nisibis, and then Amorium, with each monk advising him to go to the next, until he reached the final monk in Amorium.

When death drew near for the last monk, Salman asked him: "To whom do you advise me to go? And what do you command me to do?" The monk replied: "O my son, by Allah, I do not know of anyone on the face of the earth who holds firmly to what we were upon. However, a time has cast its shadow in which a prophet will emerge in the land of the Arabs, sent with the religion of Abraham. He will emigrate from his land to a land between two lava tracts rich in date palms, and he has unmistakable signs: he eats the gift but does not eat charity, and between his shoulders is the Seal of Prophethood. If you are able to reach that land, then do so."

After the monk passed away, Salman stayed in Amorium for a time until a group of Arab merchants from the tribe of Kalb passed by. He asked them to take him with him to the land of the Arabs in exchange for his cows and sheep. They agreed, but they betrayed him in Wadi al-Qura and sold him to a Jewish man. Later, a cousin of his from Banu Qurayzah bought him and took him to Yathrib, where he recognized the date palms described by his companion in Amorium, recognizing the city by that very description.

When the Prophet (ﷺ) emigrated to Yathrib, Salman was working in the date palms of his master. He heard his master speaking about the arrival of a man from Makkah who claimed to be a prophet. Salman was deeply shaken and descended hastily to verify the news.

After confirming the arrival of the Prophet (ﷺ), he took some dates he had gathered, went to him, and said: "It has reached me that you are a righteous man, and you have companions with you who are strangers in need. This is something I had for charity, and I saw that you are more deserving of it than others." He placed the dates near him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Eat..." but withheld his hand and did not eat. Salman said to himself: "This is one."

Then he returned to him with more dates and said: "I saw that you do not eat charity, and this is a gift I am honoring you with." The Prophet (ﷺ) ate from it and commanded his companions to eat with him. Salman said to himself: "This is the second."

Then he came to him at Baqi al-Gharqad while the Prophet (ﷺ) was burying one of his companions. He greeted him, then stepped around to look at his back, hoping to see the seal described by his companion in Amorium. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him looking at his back, he understood his purpose and cast his garment off his back. Salman looked and saw the seal, recognized it, and fell upon it, kissing it and weeping.

The Prophet (ﷺ) asked him: "What is your story?!" So Salman related his story to him, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was amazed by it and pleased that his companions should hear it from him. Thus, Salman al-Farsi embraced Islam, became one of the finest Companions, participated in many battles, and played a prominent role in digging the trench during the Battle of the Confederates (Al-Ahzab), to the extent that the Prophet (ﷺ) said of him: "Salman is one of us, the People of the House." He lived as an ascetic and a scholar until Allah took his soul, may Allah be pleased with him.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Sincerity in seeking the truth guides one to the light; whoever is sincere in his intention to seek it, Allah will grant him success in finding it.
2. Patience and perseverance along the path of faith; no matter how long the journey or how numerous the challenges, the ultimate outcome belongs to the righteous.
3. Sacrificing everything precious and valuable for the sake of belief; worldly life is nothing compared to the pleasure of Allah.
4. The importance of knowledge, learning from righteous people, and benefiting from their guidance along the journey of life.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Are you ready to sacrifice your comfort and gains in pursuit of the truth and holding fast to it, just as Salman (may Allah be pleased with him) did? And how can your personal journey toward Allah become more sincere and profound?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, research a truth about your religion that you did not know, reflect upon it deeply, or read the biography of one of the Rabbani scholars to draw inspiration from their knowledge and deeds.

title: From Fierce Enmity to Immense Loyalty
subtitle: The story of the knight of Quraysh who transformed from one of the fiercest enemies of Islam into a heroic warrior in its cause.
person: Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl (May Allah be pleased with him)
heroQuote: «Ikrimah will come to you as a believer and a muhajir (emigrant). Do not insult his father, for insulting the dead harms the living and does not reach the dead.»
intention: Read today's journey to ponder the vastness of Islamic mercy, the power of faith to transform hearts, and to draw inspiration from Ikrimah's courage and steadfastness after repentance.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl al-Makhzumi grew up in Makkah in one of the most prestigious, wealthy, and noble households of Quraysh. His father, Abu Jahl, was the master of Quraysh and the leader of supreme polytheism. Ikrimah inherited courage and equestrian skills from his father, but he also inherited an intense hostility toward Islam and the Muslims. He was one of the fiercest opponents of the call of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and one of the prominent horsemen of Quraysh who stood in the way of the truth.

steps.title: The Knight of Quraysh: From Enmity to Martyrdom
steps.content:
His father's leadership drove him to oppose the Prophet (ﷺ). He was intensely hostile to the Messenger and severely harmed his companions. Ikrimah participated in the Battle of Badr alongside his father, who led the polytheist army, and he witnessed his father's death as the spears of the Muslims drank his blood. He returned to Makkah after the defeat, and this event planted in his heart a deep desire to avenge his father against Islam.

On the day of Uhud, Ikrimah went out with his wife, Umm Hakim, and took his position on the right flank of the cavalry of Quraysh. He fought valiantly, contributing to the victory of the polytheists. In the Battle of the Trench, frustrated by the siege, he spurred his horse across the trench and crossed it in a daring maneuver.

At the Conquest of Makkah, Quraysh realized they had no power against Muhammad and his companions and decided to clear the path for him. However, Ikrimah and a group with him defied the consensus and confronted the Islamic army. Khalid ibn al-Walid defeated them, and Ikrimah fled to Yemen, having no other refuge.

Meanwhile, his wife Umm Hakim, Hind bint Utbah, and ten other women went to the Prophet (ﷺ) to give him their pledge of allegiance. Umm Hakim embraced Islam and asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for a guarantee of safety for her husband Ikrimah, to which he replied (ﷺ): "He is safe."

Umm Hakim set out in search of Ikrimah and found him on the coast of Tihamah negotiating with a Muslim boatman to transport him. The boatman was telling him: "Purify your faith so that I may transport you." Ikrimah asked: "How do I purify my faith?" He replied: "You say, 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'" Ikrimah said: "I only fled from this."

At that moment, Umm Hakim arrived and said to him: "O cousin, I have come to you from the best of people, the most righteous of people, the best of people—from Muhammad ibn Abdullah. I have sought safety for you from him, and he has granted it, so do not destroy yourself." She continued to reassure and comfort him until he returned with her.

When Ikrimah drew near Makkah, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl will come to you as a believer and an emigrant, so do not insult his father, for insulting the dead harms the living and does not reach the dead."

It was only a short while before Ikrimah and his wife arrived where the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw him, he sprang up to him in joy, without his cloak. Ikrimah stood before him and said: "O Muhammad, Umm Hakim has told me that you granted me safety." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have spoken the truth, you are safe."

Then Ikrimah asked him: "What do you call to, O Muhammad?" The Prophet (ﷺ) explained all the pillars of Islam. Ikrimah said: "By Allah, you have only called to the truth and commanded what is good. By Allah, even before you called to what you called to, you were among us the most truthful in speech and the most righteous in righteousness." Then he extended his hand and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that You are His slave and His Messenger."

After his Islam, he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to seek forgiveness for him for every act of hostility he had shown, every journey he had undertaken to extinguish the light of Allah, and everything he had said against his honor. The Prophet (ﷺ) supplicated for him: "O Allah, forgive him every enmity he showed me, and every journey he took to a place intending by it to extinguish Your light, and forgive him what he said against my honor to my face or in my absence." Ikrimah's face lit up with joy, and he said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I will not leave a single penny that I spent in hindering from the path of Allah except that I will spend twice as much in the path of Allah, nor a single battle I fought hindering from the path of Allah except that I will fight twice as many in the path of Allah."

Ikrimah fulfilled his pledge. The Muslims did not engage in any battle after his Islam without him participating in it, nor did they go out on any expedition without him being at the vanguard. On the day of Yarmouk, he rushed into battle like a thirsty person rushing to cold water. When distress intensified for the Muslims, he dismounted his horse, broke the sheath of his sword, and plunged deep into the ranks of the Byzantines. Khalid ibn al-Walid tried to stop him, but Ikrimah said: "Leave me be, O Khalid... You had an early precedence with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whereas my father and I were among the harshest of people against the Messenger of Allah, so let me make amends for what has passed." Then he called out to the Muslims: "Who will pledge to die?" His cousin Al-Harith ibn Hisham and Dirar ibn al-Azwar pledged allegiance to him, along with four hundred Muslims, and they fought fiercely.

When the Battle of Yarmouk cleared, Ikrimah, Al-Harith ibn Hisham, and Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah were found stretched upon the ground, severely wounded. Al-Harith asked for water to drink, but when it was brought to him, Ikrimah looked at it and said: "Give it to him." When they brought it near Al-Harith, he looked at Ayyash and said: "Give it to him." But by the time they reached Ayyash, he had already passed away. When they returned to his two companions, they found that they too had passed away, may Allah be pleased with them all. May He quench their thirst from the Basin of Al-Kawthar with a drink after which they will never thirst again, and grant them the lush gardens of Al-Firdaws to dwell in forever.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. The vastness of Islamic mercy and its acceptance of repentant people no matter how great their sins; the door of repentance is always open.
2. The power of faith in transforming the fiercest enemies into the most loyal allies, for guidance is in the hand of Allah alone.
3. Courage and boldness in defending the truth after recognizing it, and sacrificing self and wealth in its cause.
4. The importance of the role of a righteous wife in guiding her husband and her earnest efforts to save him from straying.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Do you believe that the door of repentance is always open, and that Allah is capable of transforming the heart of any human being no matter how rebellious they have become? And how can you be a cause for someone else's guidance, or strive to correct your path if you have been in the wrong?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Pray today for the guidance of someone you know who is straying from the path of Allah, remembering that Allah guides whom He wills, or renew your repentance from an old sin and covenant with yourself to remain steadfast.

title: From the Knight of Horses to the Knight of Goodness
subtitle: The journey of a courageous knight from the jahiliyyah of equestrian pride to the light of Islam, and a prophetic testimony that changed his name and destiny.
person: Zayd ibn Muhhalil al-Ta'i (Zayd al-Khayr) (May Allah be pleased with him)
heroQuote: «Rather, you are Zayd al-Khayr (Zayd of Goodness), not Zayd al-Khayl (Zayd of Horses). All praise is due to Allah who brought you from your plain and your mountain, and softened your heart to Islam» ﷺ
intention: Read today's journey to ponder how faith transforms hearts, how courage can be a bridge to the truth, and how life may be short yet its impact eternal.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Zayd ibn Muhhalil al-Ta'i, known in the pre-Islamic era as "Zayd al-Khayl" (Zayd of the Horses), was an unmatched knight, an eloquent poet, and a revered leader of the Banu Tayy tribe. He was renowned for his immense physical strength, a generosity that rivaled that of his father Hatim al-Ta'i, and an unwavering courage in the battlefields. His life before Islam was the embodiment of Arab chivalry and honor, yet his heart yearned for a light that would guide his soul to something loftier and more enduring.

steps.title: From Horses to Goodness
steps.content:
News of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) reached the ears of Zayd al-Khayr, so he prepared his mount and called upon the leaders of his people to visit Yathrib and meet the Prophet (ﷺ). The delegation arrived in Madinah and found the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivering a sermon from the pulpit. His words awed them, and they were amazed by the Muslims' attachment to him and their attentive listening.

No sooner had the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his sermon than Zayd al-Khayr stood up among the gathering of Muslims. He was one of the most handsome and tallest of men, to the extent that his legs grazed the ground while he was mounted on his horse. He raised his booming voice and said: "O Muhammad, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that you are His Messenger."

The noble Messenger (ﷺ) approached him and asked: "Who are you?" He replied: "I am Zayd al-Khayr ibn Muhhalil." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Rather, you are Zayd al-Khayr, not Zayd al-Khayl. All praise is due to Allah who brought you from your plain and your mountain, and softened your heart to Islam."

Zayd al-Khayr rejoiced at this prophetic title and offered to provide the Prophet (ﷺ) with three hundred horsemen to raid the lands of the Romans with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) admired his high ambition and said: "May Allah bless you, O Zayd... What a fine man you are!"

Zayd and those with him from his people embraced Islam. When he prepared to return to his homeland in Najd, the Prophet (ﷺ) bade him farewell, saying: "What a fine man this is! How much status he would have had if he had been spared the plague of Madinah!" Madinah at that time was plagued by fever, and no sooner had Zayd al-Khayr departed from it than the fever struck him. He asked his companions to keep him away from the lands of Qays, saying: "There used to be zealotries of pre-Islamic ignorance between us, and by Allah, I will not fight a Muslim until I meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

Zayd al-Khayr continued his journey toward the lands of his people, even though the grip of the fever grew harsher upon him hour after hour. He hoped to meet his people and that Allah would write Islam for them at his hands. He kept racing death while death raced him, but death soon outpaced him, and he breathed his last breath along the road. Between his Islam and his death, there was no opportunity to commit a sin. Thus, the knight of horses transformed into the knight of goodness, leaving an eternal mark in the history of Islam.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Swift response to the truth and hesitation-free acceptance when its clear proofs appear.
2. The importance of a kind word and its profound impact in transforming hearts and directing them toward goodness.
3. The virtue of one who dies upon Islam shortly after embracing it, with sincere intention for Allah.
4. The value of courage and chivalry when harnessed in the path of Allah, transforming from earthly power into spiritual strength.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can a strong and influential personality transform completely upon encountering the truth? And what are the "horses" in our lives that we must transform into "goodness" by harnessing them in the obedience of Allah and the service of His religion?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, try to be a cause of positive change in someone's life through a kind word or a good deed, drawing inspiration from Zayd al-Khayr's transformation from Zayd al-Khayl, and how faith directs energies toward the highest goals.

title: From the Chieftain of Tayy to a Knight of Islam
subtitle: The journey of Adi ibn Hatim, from fierce hostility toward Islam to unwavering faith, guided by true prophecies that opened his heart.
person: Adi ibn Hatim at-Ta'i (May Allah be pleased with him)
heroQuote: "O Adi, you possess two qualities that Allah and His Messenger love: deliberation and gentleness." ﷺ
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on the power of calm dialogue, the truth of prophecies, and how gentleness and deliberation open hearts to the truth, even after long-standing enmity.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Adi ibn Hatim at-Ta'i was a prominent and obeyed chieftain among his people, inheriting leadership from his father, Hatim at-Ta'i, whose name became synonymous with generosity. Adi was a Christian, and he used to collect the traditional quarter of war spoils from his people just as the kings of Arabia did. When news of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ reached him, he despised him intensely, viewing his call as a threat to his leadership and status. He remained hostile to Islam for nearly twenty years before Allah opened his chest to the truth.

steps.title: Prophecies Illuminating the Path of the Heart
steps.content:
When Islam gained strength and the Muslim armies spread across the land of the Arabs, Adi ordered his servant to prepare for him fat camels so he could travel to Syria and join his fellow Christians if he heard that Muhammad's army was approaching. One morning, his servant came to him in a panic, informing him that the cavalry of Muhammad had trampled their territory. Adi immediately got up, gathered his family and children to depart, but in his haste, left his sister behind in their homeland of Najd.

The Muslim cavalry arrived, and his sister was taken among the captives to Yathrib. There, she was placed with the captives by the door of the mosque. The Prophet ﷺ passed by her, and she stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my father has perished, and my protector is absent. Show me mercy, and may Allah show you mercy." The Prophet ﷺ asked her about her protector, and she informed him that it was Adi ibn Hatim. The Prophet ﷺ said, "The one who flees from Allah and His Messenger?!" Then he left her.

The next day, the Prophet ﷺ passed by her again, and she said the same thing to him, and he replied similarly. On the third day, she lost hope, but a man from behind him motioned to her to speak to him. She stood up and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my father has perished, and my protector is absent. Show me mercy, and may Allah show you mercy." He said, "I have done so." She asked to join her family in Syria, and he instructed her not to rush until she found someone from her people whom she trusted to take her to Syria.

When the Prophet ﷺ departed, she asked about the man who had motioned to her, and she was told it was Ali ibn Abi Talib (May Allah be pleased with him). She stayed until a caravan of her trusted people arrived. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ provided her with clothing, granted her a camel to ride, and gave her sufficient provisions, so she departed with the caravan.

When the sister returned to Adi, she recounted her story and how the Prophet ﷺ treated her, describing his generosity, gentleness, and humility. She said to him, "I swear by Allah, you should go to him quickly. If he is a prophet, the one who comes to him first has the precedence of merit; and if he is a king, you will never be humiliated in his presence, for you are who you are."

Adi prepared his provisions and set out for Medina, entering upon the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque. When the Prophet ﷺ saw him, he stood up, took him by the hand, and set off with him toward his house. On the way, a weak, elderly woman accompanied by a young boy stopped him, and he remained with them until their need was met while Adi stood watching.

When they reached the house, the Prophet ﷺ took a leather cushion stuffed with palm fibers and threw it to Adi, saying, "Sit on this." Adi felt shy and said, "Rather, you sit on it." He said, "No, you." So Adi complied and sat on it, and the Prophet ﷺ sat on the floor as there was no other cushion in the house.

The Prophet ﷺ turned to Adi and said, "Well, O Adi ibn Hatim, were you not a Rusoosi, practicing a religion between Christianity and Sabianism?" He said, "Yes." He said, "Were you not taking the quarter of the spoils from your people, taking what is not lawful for you in your religion?!" He said, "Yes." Then Adi knew that he was a sent prophet.

Then the Prophet ﷺ said to him, "Perhaps, O Adi, what prevents you from entering this religion is what you see of the poverty and need of the Muslims. By Allah, wealth will soon pour over them until no one will accept it. And perhaps what prevents you from entering this religion is what you see of the small number of Muslims and the multitude of their enemies. By Allah, you will soon hear of a woman traveling out of al-Qadisiyyah on her camel until she visits this House, fearing no one except Allah. And perhaps what prevents you from entering this religion is that you see that kingship and power are with non-Muslims. By Allah, you will soon hear of the white palaces of the land of Babylon being conquered for them, and the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz falling into their hands."

Adi exclaimed, "The treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz?!" The Prophet ﷺ said, "Yes, the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz." Upon that, Adi uttered the testimony of truth and embraced Islam.

Adi lived for a long time and witnessed the fulfillment of two of the Prophet's prophecies: he saw the woman traveling from al-Qadisiyyah on her camel fearing nothing until she reached the House, and he was among the first cavalry that raided the treasures of Kisra and took them. The third prophecy was fulfilled during the era of the ascetic Caliph Umar ibn Abdul Aziz, when wealth overflowed among the Muslims to the extent that the caller would announce for someone to take charity funds, and he would find no one.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. The impact of good treatment and mercy in attracting hearts to Islam, as seen with Adi's sister.
2. The power of calm dialogue and wisdom in calling to Allah, and how humility opens closed hearts.
3. The truth of the Prophet's prophecies as conclusive proof of his prophethood, establishing certainty in hearts.
4. The virtue of deliberation and gentleness in dealing with others, and how these are qualities loved by Allah and His Messenger.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can our perspective on the truth change when we encounter it with an open heart, even if preceded by hostility or misunderstanding? And what qualities do we wish to cultivate within ourselves to be beloved to Allah and His Messenger, such as deliberation and gentleness?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, try to embody deliberation and gentleness in your handling of a difficult situation or someone who disagrees with you, remembering the Prophet's advice to Adi and how these traits were the cause of his guidance.

title: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari: Sincerity of Faith and Asceticism in the World
subtitle: The journey of a noble Companion who was the most truthful in speech and the most ascetic in living, with no desire for the world, his heart attached to the Hereafter.
person: Jundub ibn Junadah al-Ghifari (Abu Dharr al-Ghifari)
heroQuote: "Neither the earth has supported nor the sky has shadowed a man more truthful than Abu Dharr." ﷺ
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on sincere faith, profound asceticism, courage in speaking the truth, and how one's entire life can be dedicated to Allah alone.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: In the valley of 'Waddan', where the tribe of 'Ghifar' lived on meager caravan trade, Jundub ibn Junadah, known as Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, grew up. He was characterized by boldness of heart, soundness of intellect, and deep foresight. He deeply resented the idols worshipped by his people besides Allah, condemning the corruption of religion and the triviality of their beliefs, while eagerly awaiting the appearance of a new prophet to fill minds and hearts with light and guidance.

steps.title: The Quest for Truth and Declaration of Islam
steps.content:
When news of the new Prophet in Mecca reached Abu Dharr, he sent his brother Anis to investigate. Anis returned describing the man as one who called to noble character, whose speech was not poetry, though people called him a magician or a soothsayer. This did not quench Abu Dharr's thirst, so he decided to go to Mecca himself, carrying a water skin, cautious of Quraysh and their brutality.

Abu Dharr arrived in Mecca and lay down in the Mosque. Ali ibn Abi Talib (May Allah be pleased with him) passed by him, recognized that he was a stranger, and hosted him for two nights without asking about his purpose. On the third night, Ali asked him, and Abu Dharr told him of his intention to meet the new Prophet. Ali's face lit up and he said, "By Allah, he is truly the Messenger of Allah." Then he led him to the house of the Prophet ﷺ.

Abu Dharr entered upon the Prophet ﷺ and greeted him with the Islamic greeting, becoming the first to greet the Prophet with it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ invited him to Islam and recited the Quran to him, and Abu Dharr readily declared the word of truth and entered the new religion, making him the fourth or fifth person to accept Islam. The Prophet ﷺ advised him not to tell anyone about his Islam out of fear for his safety, but Abu Dharr insisted on proclaiming the truth openly. He went to the Mosque and shouted at the top of his voice: "O assembly of Quraysh, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Scarcely had his words touched their ears when they panicked and rushed toward him, beating him until he was nearly dead, until al-Abbas ibn Abdul Muttalib rescued him from them.

After recovering, he returned to the Prophet ﷺ, who said to him, "Did I not forbid you from declaring your Islam?" Abu Dharr replied, "O Messenger of Allah, it was a need in my soul which I fulfilled." Then the Prophet ﷺ instructed him to return to his people and invite them to Allah. Abu Dharr returned to his tribe, where his brother Anis and his mother embraced Islam, followed by many from Ghifar, and prayer was established among them. Abu Dharr stayed in the desert with his people until the battles of Badr, Uhud, and Khandaq had passed, then he came to Medina and devoted himself to the service of the Messenger ﷺ, who favored and honored him.

After the death of the Prophet ﷺ, Abu Dharr could not bear staying in Medina and traveled to the desert of Syria. During the caliphate of Uthman (May Allah be pleased with him), he settled in Damascus and saw Muslims turning toward worldly life and indulging in luxury, which he denounced and condemned. Uthman summoned him to Medina, but finding it difficult to cope with people's attachment to the world—and they finding his strictness burdensome—Uthman instructed him to move to 'Rabadhah', a small village near Medina. Abu Dharr moved there and lived far from people, ascetic toward worldly gains, holding fast to the path of the Messenger and his two companions in preferring the everlasting over the fleeting.

A man visited him once and found no furnishings in his house, so he asked, "O Abu Dharr, where are your belongings?!" He replied, "We have a house there (meaning the Hereafter) to which we send our best belongings." In the thirty-second year after Hijrah, Abu Dharr al-Ghifari passed away—the devoted worshipper and ascetic, concerning whom the Messenger ﷺ said: "Neither the earth has supported nor the sky has shadowed a man more truthful than Abu Dharr."

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Courage in proclaiming the truth without fearing the blame of any critic, even if it contradicts the advice of close ones.
2. True asceticism in worldly life and attachment to the Hereafter, viewing this world merely as a passage rather than a permanent home.
3. Absolute truthfulness in speech and action, which earned him the praise of the Prophet ﷺ.
4. The importance of calling to Allah through good example, and how one person can influence an entire tribe.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can I apply Abu Dharr's asceticism and truthfulness in my daily life, making the Hereafter my greatest concern, and being courageous in speaking the truth and calling to it?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will review my expenses and try to give charity with something I love, and I will strive to speak the truth even if it is bitter, remembering that this world is fleeting and the Hereafter is eternal.

title: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum: The Insight of Faith and the Resolve of Jihad
subtitle: A noble Companion, blind in sight yet seeing with his heart, who set the finest examples of faith, patience, sacrifice, and devotion to the religion of Allah.
heroQuote: "He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came unto him." (Surah Abasa)
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on the power of faith that transcends physical obstacles, and how sincerity elevates its bearer to the highest ranks.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, the muezzin of the Messenger ﷺ, was a Meccan Qurayshi tied to the Prophet ﷺ by kinship, as he was the maternal cousin of the Mother of the Believers, Khadijah (May Allah be pleased with her). He was born blind, but Allah opened his heart to faith, making him among the foremost in embracing Islam. He suffered from the persecution and brutality of Quraysh, but his faith never wavered nor did his resolve weaken; instead, it made him more steadfast in Allah's religion and attached to His Noble Book.

steps.title: From Quranic Reprimand to the Honor of Martyrdom
steps.content:
Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum's eagerness for the Prophet ﷺ and his keenness to memorize the Quran were such that he missed no opportunity. One day, the Messenger ﷺ was negotiating with the chieftains of Quraysh, calling them to Islam, when Ibn Umm Maktum came seeking a verse from the Book of Allah to be recited to him, saying, "O Messenger of Allah, teach me from what Allah has taught you." The Messenger ﷺ turned away from him, frowned in his face, and turned toward those men, hoping for their Islam. As soon as the Prophet ﷺ finished speaking, Allah withheld his sight and revealed to him the words: ﴿He frowned and turned away * Because the blind man came unto him * And what would make you perceive that perhaps he might be purified * Or be reminded and the remembrance would benefit him? * As for the one who thinks himself self-sufficient * To him you give attention * And not upon you [is any blame] if he will not be purified * But as for the one who came to you striving * While he fears [Allah] * From him you are distracted * No! Indeed, it is a reminder﴾. Sixteen verses were revealed concerning him, and they continue to be recited to this day. From that day on, the Messenger ﷺ never ceased honoring his status, drawing him close to his assembly, and asking about his affairs.

When the persecution of Quraysh intensified, Allah permitted the Muslims to emigrate, and Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was among the quickest of people to leave his homeland. He and Mus'ab ibn Umair were the first of the Prophet's companions to arrive in Medina, and they set about visiting the people, reciting the Quran to them and teaching them jurisprudence in the religion of Allah. When the Messenger ﷺ arrived in Medina, he appointed him and Bilal ibn Rabah as muezzins for the Muslims; Bilal would make the call at night to wake the people, while Ibn Umm Maktum would watch for the dawn so as not to miss it. Such was the Prophet's honor for him that he appointed him to lead Medina in his absence over ten times.

After the Battle of Badr, Quranic verses were revealed elevating the status of the mujahideen and favoring them over those who stayed behind. This deeply affected Ibn Umm Maktum, and it weighed heavily on him to be deprived of this virtue, so he said, "O Messenger of Allah, if I were able to partake in Jihad, I would." He prayed to Allah with a humble heart to reveal a Quranic verse concerning him and his likes who were hindered by physical impediments from participating in Jihad. Allah answered his prayer, and the verse of exemption was revealed: ﴿Not equal are the believers remaining [at home] - other than the disabled﴾. Although Allah excused him, his ambitious soul refused to sit with those who stayed behind, and he resolved to strive in the cause of Allah. He made sure not to miss any battle, saying, "Set me up between the two ranks and hand me the banner; I will carry it for you and guard it, for I am blind and cannot flee." In the fourteenth year after Hijrah, during the decisive Battle of Qadisiyyah, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum set out with the Muslim armies, wearing his armor, fully equipped, and volunteering to carry the banner of the Muslims. The two armies met during harsh days, and the battle concluded with a resounding victory for the Muslims. Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum was found lying fallen, stained with his blood while embracing the banner of the Muslims, a martyr in the path of Allah.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. The importance of eagerness to seek knowledge and the Quran regardless of circumstances and physical obstacles.
2. The power of faith that drives its bearer to sacrifice and Jihad despite being legally excused.
3. The humility of the Prophet ﷺ and his acceptance of the divine reprimand, teaching us the importance of humility and returning to the truth.
4. The status of people with special needs in Islam and the appreciation of their efforts, proving that physical disability does not prevent one from attaining the highest ranks.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What obstacles do I think prevent me from drawing closer to Allah or serving my religion, and how can I overcome them with faith and steadfastness like Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will strive to read a portion of the Quran with contemplation, and I will look for a way to serve my religion and community despite any challenges I face, remembering that sincere resolve works miracles.

title: The Hero of the Tunnels and the Knight of Qadisiyyah
subtitle: The journey of an unmatched knight who breached fortresses, faced champions in the path of Allah, and ascended as a martyr.
person: Majza'ah ibn Thawr as-Sudusi رضي الله عنه
heroQuote: “Majza'ah ibn Thawr was a fierce champion who killed one hundred polytheists in single combat. Imagine what he did in the thick of the battle!” [The Historians]
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on the courage of the heroes who conquered al-Mada'in, their sacrifices that changed the course of history, and how bravery in the path of Allah was a path to honor and martyrdom.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Majza'ah ibn Thawr as-Sudusi was a master among the leaders of Banu Bakr, an obeyed chieftain among his people, and a fierce, fearless knight. He grew up in an authentic Arab environment characterized by chivalry and courage, making him one of the earliest to answer the call of truth and join the armies of Islam. He became one of its distinguished heroes, writing the finest pages of history with his pure blood.

steps.title: The Storming of Tustar and the End of a Hero
steps.content:
After the victory of the Muslims at Qadisiyyah, the glorious heroes yearned for further battles to continue the momentum of conquests. The Commander of the Faithful, Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه, sent orders to his governor, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari رضي الله عنه, to head towards al-Ahwaz to pursue Hurmuzanan, the commander of the Persian armies, and to liberate the fortified city of Tustar. The Caliph specifically mentioned Majza'ah ibn Thawr, commanding Abu Musa to bring him along due to his well-known courage and valor.

The Muslim army set out, with Majza'ah on the left wing, liberating cities and clearing out strongholds, while Hurmuzan fled before them until he reached Tustar, an ancient city fortified by a massive wall and a moat that was difficult to cross. The Muslims besieged Tustar for eighteen months, during which they fought eighty battles, starting with single combat and turning into fierce warfare. Majza'ah performed exceptionally in these duels, stunning minds by slaying one hundred elite enemy knights in single combat, making his name strike fear into the ranks of the Persians.

Distress intensified for the Muslims. While Abu Musa was gazing at the wall, an arrow fell before him carrying a message from a Persian noble offering to reveal a secret underground passage into the city in exchange for safety for himself and his family, after Hurmuzan had killed his brother and seized his wealth. Abu Musa granted him safety, then summoned Majza'ah ibn Thawr, confided in him about the matter, and asked him for a man of intelligence, resolve, and swimming ability. Majza'ah said, 'Make me that man, O Commander!' Abu Musa agreed.

Majza'ah set out with his Persian guide under the cover of darkness, entering an underground tunnel connecting the river to the city. The tunnel narrowed and widened, requiring Majza'ah to swim at times and wade through water at others. When they reached the outlet, Majza'ah saw Hurmuzan and intended to kill him, but he remembered Abu Musa's instruction not to initiate anything. He reined in his impulse and returned to inform Abu Musa.

Abu Musa prepared three hundred of the bravest Muslim soldiers, most skilled in swimming, and placed Majza'ah in command. Majza'ah instructed them to lighten their garments and tie their swords to their bodies. They set out in the first third of the night, battling the hazards of the perilous tunnel. By the time they reached the outlet, the tunnel had swallowed two hundred and twenty men, leaving only eighty.

As soon as Majza'ah and his companions set foot inside the city, they drew their swords, pounced on the fortress guards, rushed to the gates, and opened them while shouting 'Allahu Akbar.' Their takbeer met the takbeer of their brothers outside, and the Muslims flooded into the city at dawn. A fierce battle ensued. In the heat of battle, Majza'ah spotted Hurmuzan, headed straight for him, and engaged him with his sword. The two men clashed, each striking a fatal blow to the other. Majza'ah's sword deflected while Hurmuzan's struck Majza'ah, and the heroic champion fell lifeless on the battlefield, a martyr in the path of Allah. Hurmuzan was taken captive, and the bearers of good news carried the tidings of victory to al-Faruq, along with heartfelt condolences for his valiant knight, Majza'ah ibn Thawr رضي الله عنه.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. **Courage and Valor**: Majza'ah ibn Thawr demonstrated supreme courage in single duels and storming dangerous tunnels, teaching us the importance of boldness in standing for the truth and facing challenges without fear.
2. **Obedience and Discipline**: Despite seeing Hurmuzan—the killer of his brother—Majza'ah restrained himself and adhered to the instructions of his commander, Abu Musa, emphasizing the value of obedience and discipline in teamwork and leadership.
3. **Sacrifice and Devotion**: His readiness to enter the perilous tunnel and offer his life as a martyr for the sake of Allah embodies the highest meanings of sacrifice for the supremacy of the truth.
4. **Utilizing Opportunities and Military Intelligence**: The Muslim commanders' ability to exploit intelligence (the Persian's message) and plan to infiltrate the city through a secret gateway demonstrates military intelligence and sound management.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can I draw inspiration from the courage of Majza'ah ibn Thawr to face the challenges of my life, make sacrifices for my principles and values, and remain obedient to the truth and righteous leadership?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will look for an opportunity to perform an act that requires courage or boldness in the cause of truth—whether speaking a word of truth, offering help to someone in need, or overcoming a personal challenge with reliance on Allah.

title: The Knight of the Quran and the Companion of the Angels
subtitle: The journey of the master of Aws whose recitation the angels listened to, becoming a light that guided hearts and illuminated paths.
person: Usaid ibn Hudair رضي الله عنه
emotion: Faith, Reverence, Love for the Quran, Wisdom
heroQuote: “Those were the angels listening to you, O Usaid... Had you continued your recitation, the people would have seen them and they would not have remained hidden.” [Muhammad the Messenger of Allah ﷺ]
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on the depth of faith and the beauty of the Quran, how it touches hearts and draws souls even among the angels, and to draw inspiration from Usaid's wisdom in seeking the truth.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Usaid ibn Hudair رضي الله عنه was one of the masters and nobles of Aws in Yathrib, nicknamed 'Al-Kamil' (The Perfect) due to his sound intellect, noble lineage, beautiful character, and skill in horsemanship and archery, in addition to being a literate person in a society where reading and writing were rare. He held a magnificent status among his people, consulted in matters, and known for his wisdom and gravity.

steps.title: The Islam of Usaid and the Recitation of the Angels
steps.content:
In the first missionary delegation in Islamic history, the Makkan youth Mus'ab ibn Umair رضي الله عنه arrived in Yathrib and stayed as a guest of As'ad ibn Zurarah رضي الله عنه, one of the nobles of Khazraj. Mus'ab made As'ad's home his headquarters, launching from it to spread the call of Allah and preach His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The youth of Yathrib flocked to Mus'ab's gatherings, enticed by the sweetness of his speech, clarity of his arguments, gentleness of his manners, and the radiance of faith shining from his face. Above all, they were drawn to his recitation of the Quran with his tender, soulful voice.

Word reached Usaid ibn Hudair and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh رضي الله عنهما, the two masters of Aws. Sa'd said to Usaid, 'May you be bereft of your mother, O Usaid! Go to this Makkan youth who has come to our homes to deceive our weak ones and mock our gods, and rebuke him, warning him never to set foot in our lands again.' Usaid took his spear and headed toward the orchard where Mus'ab and As'ad were sitting. When As'ad saw him approaching, he said to Mus'ab, 'Woe to you, O Mus'ab! This is the master of his people, the soundest of them in intellect and the most complete. If he accepts Islam, many will follow him. Be truthful with Allah regarding him and handle him gently.'

Usaid stood before the gathering, turned to Mus'ab and his companion, and shouted, 'What brought you both to our lands, and what enticed you to our weak ones?! Leave this neighborhood if you value your lives.' Mus'ab turned to Usaid with a face radiant with the light of faith and addressed him with sincere, captivating tone, 'O master of his people, would you care for something better?' Usaid asked, 'And what is that?' Mus'ab said, 'You sit with us and listen to us; if you are pleased with what we say, you accept it, and if you dislike it, we will move away from you and not return.'

Usaid replied, 'You have been fair.' He planted his spear in the ground and sat down. Mus'ab began explaining the reality of Islam to him and reciting verses of the Quran. Usaid's face lit up with joy, and he said, 'How wonderful is this speech, and how majestic is what you recite!' He asked how to enter Islam. Mus'ab told him, 'Take a bath, purify your clothes, testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and pray two rak'ahs.' Usaid went to the well, purified himself with water, testified to the twin declarations of faith, prayed two rak'ahs, and on that day joined the ranks of Islam as one of the prominent Arab knights. His Islam became the cause for the Islam of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, followed by masses of Aws, turning Madinah into the migration destination and sanctuary for the great Islamic state.

Usaid ibn Hudair fell passionately in love with the Quran, like a lover devoted to his beloved. He was never seen except striving in jihad or devotedly reciting the Book of Allah with his tender, affectionate voice. In the dead of night, Usaid was sitting in his threshing floor with his horse tied nearby and his son Yahya sleeping beside him. His heart yearned to recite the Quran, so he began reciting verses from Surah al-Baqarah. Suddenly, his horse began to circle and violently agitate whenever he recited, and calm down whenever he stopped. He repeated this several times, fearing for his son Yahya lest the horse trample him, so he went to wake him up. When he looked up at the sky, he saw a cloud resembling a canopy—the eye had never seen anything more magnificent or splendid—hung with things like lamps, filling the horizon with light and radiance, rising upwards until it disappeared from his sight. In the morning, he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and related what he had seen. The Prophet ﷺ said to him, 'Those were the angels listening to you, O Usaid... Had you continued your recitation, the people would have seen them and they would not have remained hidden.'

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. **The Power and Impact of the Quran**: It demonstrates how reciting the Holy Quran in a reverent voice can touch hearts, transform souls, and even attract angels to listen.
2. **Wisdom in Calling to Allah**: The story of Mus'ab ibn Umair and Usaid ibn Hudair highlights the importance of calm dialogue and fair presentation of the truth rather than confrontation and harshness.
3. **Seeking Truth and Fairness**: Despite his status and authority, Usaid ibn Hudair was fair in listening to Mus'ab, showing his noble character and sincere desire to know the truth.
4. **The Blessing of Faith and Good Role Modeling**: Usaid's Islam was a magnificent turning point, followed by the masters of his people and then vast crowds, emphasizing the importance of a good role model in spreading goodness and guidance.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What is the extent of my connection to the Holy Quran? How can I make its recitation and contemplation an inseparable part of my daily life to feel its blessings and impact on my heart, and be a cause for guiding others?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will set aside time to recite a portion of the Holy Quran with contemplation and reverence, and I will try to listen to a heartfelt recitation by a reciter, meditating on the meanings of the verses, hoping Allah grants me the blessing of listening and the sweetness of faith.

title: Abdullah ibn Abbas: The Sage of the Ummah and Interpreter of the Quran
subtitle: The journey of the youthful elder whom Allah blessed with wisdom, becoming an ocean of knowledge and a beacon of guidance.
person: Abdullah ibn Abbas رضي الله عنه
heroQuote: “O Allah, grant him wisdom.”
intention: Read today's journey to draw inspiration from the biography of the Sage of the Ummah in seeking and spreading knowledge, and how wisdom is the key to understanding and eloquence.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Abdullah ibn Abbas رضي الله عنه was born three years before migration. He was the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the Sage of the Ummah, and the Interpreter of the Quran. From his early childhood, he was blessed by the Prophet's ﷺ supplication for him to be granted wisdom. Thus, his heart became a vessel for knowledge, his tongue eloquent, and his mind vast in comprehension. He grew up in the embrace of prophecy; the very first thing that entered his stomach was the blessed saliva of the Prophet ﷺ, filling his heart with piety and wisdom, making him attain glory from all its sides, combining the honors of companionship, kinship, knowledge, and piety.

steps.title: From Prophetic Supplication to the Wisdom of the Ummah
steps.content:
Ever since the Prophet ﷺ mixed his pure saliva for him and he reached the age of discernment, Abdullah ibn Abbas accompanied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as closely as an eye's shadow. He would prepare his water for ablution, pray behind him, and ride behind him on travels, becoming like his shadow wherever he went. Throughout all this, he carried a conscious heart, a clear mind, and a memory surpassing any recording device. He narrated that once the Prophet ﷺ intended to perform ablution, and he rushed to prepare the water. The Prophet ﷺ was pleased with what he did. On another occasion, when the Prophet ﷺ stood to pray, he gestured for him to stand alongside him, so he stood behind him. When the prayer finished, the Prophet leaned over and said, 'What prevented you from standing beside me, O Abdullah?' I replied, 'You are too grand in my eyes and too noble for me to stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you, O Messenger of Allah.' The Prophet ﷺ raised his hands to the sky and supplicated, 'O Allah, grant him wisdom.' Allah answered His Prophet's prayer, and the Hashimite youth was granted a degree of wisdom that surpassed the greatest of sages.

His profound wisdom manifested in numerous situations, including his encounter with the Khawarij who had broken away from Ali ibn Abi Talib رضي الله عنه. Ali permitted him to go and speak to them. He entered upon them and found them to be people who exerted themselves immensely in worship. They asked him, 'What brings you here, O Ibn Abbas?' He said, 'I have come to speak to you.' He then asked them what grievances they held against the cousin of the Messenger of Allah, the husband of his daughter, and the first to believe in him. They mentioned three things: arbitration by men in the matter of Allah's religion, his fighting Aisha and Mu'awiyah without taking spoils or captives, and his erasing the title 'Commander of the Faithful' from his name.

He answered them with wisdom: Regarding arbitration by men, he cited a verse from Surah al-Ma'idah: ﴿Whereby two just men among you shall judge﴾ regarding hunting; how much more vital is it for preserving the lives of Muslims and reconciling between them? They agreed. Regarding his fighting Aisha and Mu'awiyah, he explained that Aisha is the Mother of the Believers—did they wish to capture their own mother and treat her as lawful spoils? They agreed. Regarding his erasing the title 'Commander of the Faithful', he reminded them of the Prophet's action on the Day of Hudaybiyyah when the polytheists asked him to erase the title 'Messenger of Allah' from the treaty. The Prophet ﷺ did so while saying, 'By Allah, I am the Messenger of Allah even if you deny me.' They agreed to this as well. Through his wisdom and decisive proofs, twenty thousand of them returned to the ranks of Ali رضي الله عنه.

Ibn Abbas did not merely seek knowledge; he humbled himself for it. If news of a hadith reached him from a Companion, he would go to the doorstep of his house during his afternoon nap, using his cloak as a pillow on the threshold while the wind blew dust upon him. Had he wished to ask permission, he would have been granted it, but he did this out of pure humility, saying, 'Knowledge is approached, it does not approach.' He demonstrated his humility and the high status of scholars when he held the stirrup for Zayd ibn Thabit رضي الله عنه and said, 'Thus we were commanded to do with our scholars.'

After completing his pursuit of knowledge, he transformed into a teacher educating the people, turning his home into a university for Muslims. He divided his weekly days for different sciences: a day for tafsir, a day for fiqh, a day for military expeditions (maghazi), a day for poetry, and a day for the history of the Arabs. No scholar sat with him except that he deferred to him, and no questioner asked him except that he found knowledge with him. He became an advisor to the Rightly Guided Caliphs despite his youth, and Umar ibn al-Khattab رضي الله عنه used to bring him close and say of him, 'He is the youth of elders: he has a questioning tongue and an intellect-storing heart.'

Ibn Abbas رضي الله عنه was also a preacher and reminder. Among his admonitions to those committing sins was: 'O sinner, do not feel secure from the consequence of your sin, and know that what follows the sin is greater than the sin itself.' He رضي الله عنه used to fast by day and stand in prayer by night. Abdullah ibn Mulaykah narrated that he saw him one night reading ﴿And the intoxication of death will bring the truth; that is what you were trying to avoid﴾, repeating it and weeping until dawn, bearing witness to his piety and reverence.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. The importance of seeking knowledge and humility in it: This is reflected in Ibn Abbas's tireless pursuit of knowledge from the Companions and his humility towards Zayd ibn Thabit, affirming that 'knowledge is approached, it does not approach.'
2. Wisdom in dawah and debate: Seen in his ability to convince the Khawarij through reason and proof from the Quran and Sunnah, bringing thousands back to the truth.
3. Piety and reverence: Ibn Abbas spent his nights in prayer and fasting, weeping out of fear of Allah, showing the depth of his faith and emotional connection to the Quran.
4. The responsibility of a scholar toward society: He did not keep knowledge to himself; rather, he turned it into an open university for the people, offered counsel, and advised the caliphs, confirming the role of scholars in leading the Ummah.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can I apply the principle of 'knowledge is approached, it does not approach' in my life? What practical steps can I take to increase my knowledge and wisdom?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, I will dedicate time to seek religious knowledge, even if modest, and I will strive for humility in learning, pondering how to use what I learn to benefit myself and those around me.

title: Tears of Awe and the Light of Knowledge
subtitle: He was among the most handsome and radiant of people, yet in the depths of the night, he wept out of fear of Allah until his tears carved two tracks down his cheeks.
heroQuote: "O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him], and enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise."
intention: Read today's journey to ponder the profound awe of Allah that defined Abdullah ibn Abbas, and how knowledge and piety adorn a human being and refine their soul.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Abdullah ibn Abbas (May Allah be pleased with them both), the cousin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, was among the most handsome and radiant of people, combining physical beauty with noble character. He grew up in the embrace of prophethood and acquired knowledge directly from the pure fountain of revelation. His life was a unique blend of outward grace and spiritual depth, making him a focal point of admiration and a paragon of knowledge and piety.

steps.title: The Sage of the Ummah and Tears of Awe
steps.content:
The beauty of Abdullah ibn Abbas (May Allah be pleased with them both) was not merely superficial; it was a reflection of his inner beauty and profound piety. He would weep in the depths of the night out of fear of Allah, until his streaming tears carved two tracks down his smooth cheeks, which some described as resembling the straps of a sandal due to the abundance of tears he shed in awe of Allah, the Exalted.

Ibn Abbas reached the pinnacle of scholarly glory, becoming known as the Sage of the Ummah and the Interpreter of the Quran. During the caliphate of Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan (May Allah be pleased with him), Mu'awiyah went out for Hajj in a grand procession of state officials, and Abdullah ibn Abbas also went for Hajj. However, Ibn Abbas's procession far outnumbered that of the Caliph, filled with seekers of knowledge who gathered around him to drink from the ocean of his knowledge.

He lived for seventy-one years, filling the world with knowledge, understanding, wisdom, and piety. When his appointed time arrived, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah performed the funeral prayer over him. As they lowered him into his grave, the mourners heard a reciter reciting the words of Allah, the Exalted: "O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and pleasing [to Him], and enter among My servants, and enter My Paradise." It was as if it were a testimony from the heavens regarding his magnificent status.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. True beauty lies in the fear of Allah and piety; no matter how handsome a person's appearance may be, the light of faith enhances their radiance.
2. Seeking knowledge and striving in it elevates a person by degrees, making them beacons that guide people, even surpassing the status of those in authority.
3. Weeping out of fear of Allah is a sign of sincere faith and a deep connection with the Creator, and it is a means to purify and cleanse the soul.
4. A good ending and divine pleasure are the ultimate goals of every believer, achieved through righteous deeds and piety in this worldly life.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can I deepen my fear of Allah, the Exalted, and ensure that the knowledge I seek becomes a light that illuminates my path and brings me closer to Him, rather than remaining merely a worldly adornment?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Dedicate a portion of your night to voluntary night prayers, even if it is just two rak'ahs. Ponder the greatness of Allah, try to cultivate awe in your heart, and then read verses of the Quran with contemplation to increase your knowledge and certainty.

title: The Conqueror of Conquests: An-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin
subtitle: The chieftain of Muzaynah who led his people to Islam, then led the Muslim armies to the 'Conqueror of Conquests' in Nahawand, sealing his life as a martyr in the path of Allah.
heroQuote: "And among the bedouin are those who believe in Allah and the Last Day and take what they spend as means of nearness to Allah and of [obtaining] the prayers of the Messenger. Unquestionably, it is a means of nearness for them. Allah will admit them into His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."
intention: Read today's journey to draw inspiration from An-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin regarding the spirit of wise leadership, courage in upholding the truth, sacrifice in the path of Allah, and how faith serves as an impetus for giving.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: An-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani was a chieftain of the Muzaynah tribe, whose homes were located near the route between Medina and Makkah. Ever since the migration of the Prophet ﷺ to Medina, news of Islam continually reached Muzaynah, and An-Nu'man and his people heard nothing of Muhammad ﷺ except goodness, mercy, kindness, and justice. An-Nu'man was a wise leader who recognized with clear insight that this new religion was the truth, and that people were rushing towards it while others lagged behind.

steps.title: From Chieftain to the Conqueror of Conquests
steps.content:
One evening, An-Nu'man gathered his brothers and the elders of his tribe, announcing his intention to go to Yathrib to meet the Prophet ﷺ, and invited whoever wished to accompany him. By morning, his ten brothers and four hundred horsemen from Muzaynah had readied themselves to go with him. An-Nu'man felt shy to visit the Prophet ﷺ without bringing a gift, but a severe, barren year of drought had left them with neither livestock nor crops. He searched his home and the homes of his brothers, gathered whatever meager flocks the drought had spared, and presented them to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, declaring his Islam and the Islam of those with him.

Yathrib rejoiced over the Islam of An-Nu'man and his companions. The Prophet ﷺ was immensely pleased, accepted their humble gift, and a verse from Surah At-Tawbah was revealed concerning them.

An-Nu'man marched under the banner of the Prophet ﷺ, witnessing all his battles, and played a decisive role in suppressing the wars of apostasy during the caliphate of Abu Bakr as-Siddiq. During the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him), An-Nu'man led a delegation to the Persian Emperor Yazdegerd, inviting him to Islam before the Battle of Qadisiyyah, delivering an eloquent address calling to the religion of Allah, or the payment of Jizyah, or battle. The Emperor flew into a rage and ordered that a load of dirt be placed upon the most noble among them. Asim ibn Umar promptly stepped forward and took it, bringing glad tidings of the impending conquest of Persian lands.

When the Persians gathered their forces to confront the Muslims in Nahawand, Umar ibn al-Khattab chose An-Nu'man to lead the army, saying, "By Allah, I will appoint over the Muslim army a man who, when the two hosts meet, will be swifter than the spears." An-Nu'man led his army brilliantly, devising a meticulous plan to counter the iron spikes planted by the Persians by feigning a retreat so the Persians would remove them. In the decisive battle, An-Nu'man made takbir three times; upon the third, he rushed forward like a fierce lion, and a fierce battle ensued, shattering the Persian army. During the battle, An-Nu'man's horse slipped in the blood, causing him to fall and sustain a fatal wound. His brother took up the standard and covered him with a cloak. When the great victory, known as the 'Conqueror of Conquests,' was achieved, the soldiers asked about their commander. His brother lifted the cloak and said, "This is your commander; Allah has fulfilled his eyes with victory and sealed his life with martyrdom."

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Wise leadership begins with sincere insight into the truth, embodied in taking the initiative towards goodness and inviting people to it.
2. Sacrificing wealth and self in the path of Allah is a sign of sincere faith and a cause for attaining Allah's pleasure and descending blessings.
3. Wisdom in calling to Allah, balancing gentleness and firmness, and clearly explaining the foundations of religion.
4. Courage and boldness in battlefields, strategic planning, and reliance on Allah are the keys to victory and empowerment.
5. Martyrdom in the path of Allah is the highest aspiration and most magnificent rank, serving as a blessed conclusion to a life filled with devotion.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can I be an influential leader in my environment, combining wisdom and courage, and making sacrifices for the principles I believe in, following the example of An-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose a charitable or community cause you believe in, take the initiative in it, try to rally people around it, and contribute whatever effort or wealth you can to ensure its success.

title: Profitable is the Transaction, O Abu Yahya
subtitle: An Arab youth enslaved by the Romans who became a wealthy merchant, then gave away all his wealth to migrate, earning the pleasure of Allah and His Messenger, verifying the Prophet's words: "Profitable is the transaction."
heroQuote: "Profitable is the transaction, O Abu Yahya! Profitable is the transaction!" - The Prophet's ﷺ words to Suhaib (May Allah be pleased with him).
intention: Read today's journey to ponder the greatness of faith that drives a person to sacrifice everything precious in the path of Allah, and how patience and certainty yield everlasting goodness.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Suhaib ibn Sinan al-Rumi was not originally Roman; rather, he was purely Arab, born to a father from the Banu Numayr and a mother from Tamim. However, destiny willed that he be taken captive as a child not exceeding five years of age when a raiding party of the Roman army attacked the village of Ath-Thani in Iraq, where his mother was residing. Suhaib was sold in the slave markets of Roman lands and passed from hand to hand, growing up there and acquiring a Roman accent, which earned him the moniker 'Al-Rumi' (the Roman).

steps.title: A Profitable Trade with Allah
steps.content:
Despite growing up in Roman lands and forgetting Arabic, his heart remained attached to his original homeland, and he never forgot that he was an Arab from the sons of the desert. His yearning increased when he heard a Christian monk prophesy the emergence of a prophet from Makkah calling to the light. An opportunity arose, and Suhaib escaped from the slavery of his masters, directing his face toward Makkah—the haven of the Arabs and the birthplace of the awaited Prophet. Suhaib entered into an alliance with Abdullah ibn Jud'an and engaged in trade, which yielded abundant wealth.

One day, Suhaib returned to Makkah and was told that Muhammad ﷺ had been sent, calling to belief in Allah. Suhaib proceeded cautiously to the house of Al-Arqam, where he met Ammar ibn Yasir. They entered together by the blessing of Allah, listened to what the Prophet ﷺ had to say, and the light of faith illuminated their chests, whereupon they declared their Islam. Suhaib endured his share of Qurayshi persecution and torture with patience and certainty, alongside Bilal, Ammar, and others, knowing that the path to Paradise is fraught with hardships.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ permitted migration to Medina, Suhaib resolved to join him, but Quraysh blocked his path and stationed guards over him to protect his wealth. Suhaib watched for an opportunity, and one night, he feigned illness. When the guards became heedless of him, he fled. Some horsemen of Quraysh pursued him, so he said to them, "You know that I am among the best archers of the people. By Allah, you will not reach me until I shoot every one of you with an arrow, and then strike you with my sword." He then offered to show them where his wealth was hidden in Makkah in exchange for letting him migrate, and they agreed. Suhaib arrived in Medina exhausted, and the Prophet ﷺ welcomed him joyfully, saying twice, "Profitable is the transaction, O Abu Yahya! Profitable is the transaction!" as if acknowledging the magnitude of his great sacrifice.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Sincere faith drives a person to sacrifice everything precious in the path of Allah, even if it means letting go of all worldly possessions.
2. Patience and steadfastness upon the truth in the face of persecution and trials are the keys to salvation and winning Allah's pleasure.
3. Attachment to the Hereafter and prioritizing it over the worldly life is the profitable trade that never fails, validated by Allah and His Messenger.
4. Nothing prevents a believer from reaching the truth, even if they were a slave or a stranger; determination and persistence overcome all obstacles.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: What sacrifices am I willing to make for the sake of my religion? Do I prioritize Allah's pleasure over worldly gains, following the example of Suhaib, who traded his worldly life to purchase his Hereafter?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Choose something you love from your wealth, time, or effort, and give it in charity or spend it in the path of Allah, invoking the intention of sacrifice and altruism, knowing that Allah blesses the little when it is done sincerely for His noble Face.

title: The Wise Ascetic: From Idol Worship to the Light of Faith
subtitle: The transformative journey of Abu ad-Darda from a heedless merchant to an ascetic scholar, defending his faith with his heart and tongue.
heroQuote: «Abu ad-Darda would ward off worldly temptations with both hands and his heart.» - Abdur-Rahman ibn Awf (May Allah be pleased with him)
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on how asceticism and the pursuit of knowledge can elevate a person to the highest ranks.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Abu ad-Darda, Uwaymir ibn Malik al-Khazraji al-Ansari, was one of the prominent merchants of Medina before Islam, renowned for his sharp intellect and wisdom. He was a close friend of Abdullah ibn Rawahah (May Allah be pleased with him). Abu ad-Darda delayed his acceptance of Islam while his friend Abdullah eagerly embraced the new faith, yet the bonds of brotherhood remained unbroken. Abdullah would frequently visit him and invite him to Islam.

steps.title: The Transformation of the Heart and the Light of Faith
steps.content:
One day, while Abu ad-Darda was at his shop, Abdullah ibn Rawahah resolved to do something momentous. He entered Abu ad-Darda's house, finding the door open and Umm ad-Darda in the courtyard. He asked permission and entered the room where Abu ad-Darda kept his idol. Pulling out an adze he had brought with him, he struck the idol, chopping it into pieces while reciting: 'Verily, every falsehood called upon besides Allah is bound to vanish...' When he finished reducing it to fragments, he left the house.

Umm ad-Darda returned to the room and was struck with horror to see the idol shattered, its pieces scattered across the floor. She began striking her cheeks in grief, crying out, 'You have ruined me, Ibn Rawahah!' Soon after, Abu ad-Darda returned home to find his wife weeping and sobbing. He asked her, 'What is the matter?' She informed him of what Abdullah ibn Rawahah had done. He looked at the idol and found it in ruins. Initially consumed by anger, he intended to seek revenge, but his fury quickly subsided. He calmed down, reflected on what had happened, and said, 'If there were any good in this idol, it would have defended itself from harm.'

Abu ad-Darda rushed off to find Abdullah ibn Rawahah, and together they went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), where Abu ad-Darda declared his submission to the religion of Allah, becoming the last of his household to embrace Islam. He believed with a faith that permeated every atom of his being, feeling profound regret for the spiritual blessings he had missed. He resolved to make up for lost time through rigorous effort, devoting himself completely to worship and thirstily pursuing sacred knowledge. Recognizing that commerce disturbed the sweetness of his worship and caused him to miss circles of knowledge, he abandoned trade without hesitation or regret.

During the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him), Umar wished to appoint him to a post in the Levant, but Abu ad-Darda refused. However, he agreed to go there to teach the people the Book of their Lord and the Sunnah of His Prophet. Upon arriving in Damascus, he found that the people had become infatuated with luxury and immersed in worldly pleasures, which shocked him. He called the people to the mosque and admonished them, saying: 'O people of Damascus, why do I see you gathering what you do not eat, building what you do not dwell in, and hoping for what you cannot attain!' The people wept so bitterly that their sobbing could be heard from outside the mosque.

Abu ad-Darda remained in Damascus, preaching to its people, reminding them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom until certainty (death) came to him. When he fell terminally ill, his companions asked him, 'What are you complaining of?' He replied, 'My sins.' They asked, 'And what do you desire?' He replied, 'The forgiveness of my Lord.' Then he instructed those around him, 'Prompt me to say: There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' He kept repeating it until his soul parted from this world.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Reflection on rational truths leads to faith, even after initial anger.
2. Asceticism in worldly matters and abandoning distractions from Allah is the path to true happiness and salvation.
3. The pursuit of knowledge and worship are the foundation for building a strong Muslim personality.
