4. Gentle admonition and reminding people of the Hereafter are among the greatest means of calling to Allah.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Does the wealth and adornment of this world distract you from the remembrance of Allah and the pursuit of knowledge, or are you striving earnestly to balance the good of this world and the Hereafter?

title: The Beloved of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): A Story of Loyalty and Destiny
subtitle: The journey of Zayd ibn Harithah from captivity to becoming the dearest person to the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ).
heroQuote: «By Allah, Zayd ibn Harithah was worthy of leadership, and he was the dearest of all people to me.» - The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on how destiny can elevate a person, and how loyalty becomes a means to attaining the love of Allah and His Messenger.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Zayd ibn Harithah al-Kalbi is the noble Companion whom the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) adopted before the revelation, and he was known as 'Zayd ibn Muhammad'. Born among the Banu Kalb, he was one of the dearest people to the heart of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Zayd's story began in his childhood when destiny decreed that he would undergo difficult trials that shaped his unique character.

steps.title: From Captivity to the Prophetic Household
steps.content:
Sa'da bint Tha'labah, Zayd's mother, had set out to visit her people, the Banu Ma'n, taking along her young son Zayd, who was about eight years old. Scarcely had she settled in her people's territory when a cavalry raid by the Banu al-Qayn attacked them, seizing property, driving away camels, and taking captive the women and children. Zayd was among those captured.

The raiders brought Zayd to the Suq Ukaz, a seasonal market held by the Arabs during the sacred months for trade. They offered him for sale, and a wealthy noble of Quraysh, Hakim ibn Hizam ibn Khuwaylid, purchased him for four hundred dirhams, along with a group of other young boys, and brought them back to Mecca.

When his aunt Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (May Allah be pleased with her) learned of his arrival, she visited him, greeting him warmly. He said to her, 'O aunt, I have bought a group of young boys from Ukaz, choose whichever you wish.' Khadijah chose Zayd and later gifted him to her husband, Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ), before his prophethood. Thus, Zayd entered the prophetic household, finding the care and love he had not found anywhere else.

Zayd lived under the care of the Prophet (ﷺ), growing up rooted in noble character, receiving boundless care and affection until the Prophet (ﷺ) loved him dearly, stating: 'By Allah, Zayd ibn Harithah was worthy of leadership, and he was the dearest of all people to me.' Zayd (May Allah be pleased with him) was the first among the freed slaves to accept Islam. He participated in numerous battles, commanded several military expeditions, and achieved martyrdom at the Battle of Mu'tah, leaving behind an inspiring legacy of loyalty, bravery, and faith.

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. Allah's decree is absolute and may carry immense good even within the most difficult circumstances.
2. Loyalty and sincerity are among the greatest traits that bring a servant closer to their Lord and the hearts of the righteous.
3. The Prophet (ﷺ) was a role model in mercy and justice, even toward those who held the status of slaves.
4. A righteous upbringing in an environment of faith is the foundation for building a strong Islamic personality.

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: How can Zayd's story inspire you to appreciate Allah's blessings upon you, and to strive for loyalty and sincerity in your relationships and dealings?

steps.title: Today's Action
steps.content: Today, strive to remain true to a promise you made, fulfill a trust placed in you, or offer a service to someone in need without expecting anything in return, following the example of Zayd's loyalty (May Allah be pleased with him).

title: An Undying Love: The Story of Zayd ibn Harithah
subtitle: A journey of loyalty and selflessness, from slavery to the heart of prophecy, and from choice to martyrdom.
person: Zayd ibn Harithah (May Allah be pleased with him)
heroQuote: «I have seen something in this man, and I will never part with him ever.»
intention: Read today's journey to reflect on the greatness of loyalty and selflessness, and how sincere love can change the course of a human life and forge an immortal hero.

steps.title: Introduction
steps.content: Zayd ibn Harithah (May Allah be pleased with him) was a young boy from the Banu Kalb who was taken captive as a small child and sold in the market of Ukaz. Lady Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (May Allah be pleased with her) purchased him and later gifted him to her husband, Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ), before he was commissioned as a prophet. Zayd grew up under the care of the Prophet (ﷺ), drinking deeply from his noble character and enjoying his precious companionship, holding a special place in his heart.

steps.title: A Love Unlike Any Other
steps.content:
Zayd's mother, heartbroken by the loss of her son, could find no peace or dry her tears; she searched for him everywhere, while his father questioned every passing caravan about the apple of his eye, even composing mournful poetry over his loss. During one of the Hajj seasons, while some members of Zayd's tribe were circumambulating the Ancient House, they caught sight of Zayd, recognized him, and he recognized them. Upon returning home, they informed Harithah of what they had seen and heard.

Harithah did not hesitate for a moment. He saddled his mount, packed enough wealth to ransom his son, brought along his brother Ka'b, and set off hastily toward Mecca. Upon arriving, they entered upon Muhammad ibn Abdullah (ﷺ) and said to him, 'O son of Abdul-Muttalib, you are the neighbors of God, you release the captive, feed the hungry, and succor the distressed. We have come to you concerning our son who is with you, and we have brought wealth to ransom him with. Do us a favor, and ransom him for whatever you wish.'

The Prophet (ﷺ) asked, 'Who is the son you are referring to?' They replied, 'Your servant Zayd ibn Harithah.' He said, 'Would you like something better than the ransom? I will call him and give him the choice: if he chooses you, he is yours without any payment, but if he chooses me, then by Allah, I am not one to turn away from someone who chooses me.'

The Prophet (ﷺ) called Zayd and asked him, 'Do you know these two?' Zayd replied, 'This is my father Harithah ibn Shurahbil, and this is my uncle Ka'b.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, 'I have given you a choice: if you wish, you may go with them, and if you wish, you may stay with me.'

Zayd did not hesitate for a second, replying without delay, 'Rather, I choose to stay with you.' His father exclaimed, 'Woe to you, Zayd! Do you choose slavery over your father and mother?!' Zayd responded with words overflowing with love and loyalty: 'I have seen something in this man, and I will never part with him ever.'

At that, the Prophet (ﷺ) took Zayd by the hand, led him out to the Sacred House, stood with him at the Hijr before a gathering of Quraysh, and announced, 'O people of Quraysh, bear witness that this is my son; he inherits from me and I inherit from him.' Thus, Zayd was known as 'Zayd ibn Muhammad' until the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent with Islam and adoption was abolished by Allah's words: ﴿Call them by their fathers' names﴾, after which he returned to being called Zayd ibn Harithah.

Zayd did not know at the time he chose the Prophet (ﷺ) over his family what immense blessings he was gaining; he went on to become the confidant of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the commander of his expeditions and military detachments. In the Battle of Mu'tah, Zayd commanded the army by order of the Prophet (ﷺ) and achieved martyrdom in the path of Allah after a heroic battle, becoming the first of the three commanders to attain martyrdom. The Prophet (ﷺ) grieved deeply for him, weeping openly with his voice raised, and said, 'This is the weeping of a lover for his beloved.'

steps.title: Lessons Learned
steps.content:
1. **The Power of Love and Selflessness**: How Zayd's love for the Prophet (ﷺ) surpassed his love for his family and homeland, demonstrating the greatness of the Prophet's character and spiritual impact.
2. **Loyalty to Covenants**: Zayd's choice to remain with the Prophet (ﷺ) despite the opportunity to return to his family and freedom highlights the value of loyalty and adherence to truth.
3. **Leadership and Sacrifice**: His assumption of the leadership of the army at Mu'tah and his martyrdom therein embody the highest meanings of bravery and sacrifice for the sake of Allah.
4. **The Status of the Companions**: The text shows how the noble Companions were unique exemplars in faith and loyalty, and how Allah honored them with the companionship of His Prophet (ﷺ).

steps.title: Reflection
steps.content: Reflect within your heart: Is there a love in your life that parallels Zayd's love for the Prophet (ﷺ)? And what sacrifices are you willing to make for your principles and highest values?

steps.content: Make today's action a moment to contemplate a great figure who positively impacted your life, try to emulate a virtue or trait from them, and make a silent supplication for them.
